book.title: The Life You Already Inherited
book.subtitle: Resurrection life, union with God, and the practice of spiritual authority
book.purpose: A teaching book that shows believers what they already inherited in Christ — resurrection life, union with the Father, unconditional love and usable spiritual authority — and how to practice it daily.
book.core_subject: A multi-session teaching corpus expounding Hebrews 2, John 17, Colossians 3, Malachi and related texts, joined to personal testimony of healing, resurrection and providence.
book.reader_journey: From inherited habit, tradition and fear of death, through scriptural exposition of destroyed death and granted union, into a disciplined practice of mind, prayer and ministry, ending in testimony and prophetic vision.
book.editorial_progression: Diagnosis of inherited religion → doctrinal foundation (resurrection life, offices, union) → interior anatomy and mental discipline → practice and testimony → corporate vision.
book.angle: Treat the corpus as a sustained correction: against legalism, rapture-fixation, performance ministry and fear of death, replaced by inheritance already granted and practiced.
book.reader: Local congregations, retreat attendees, pastors and ministers receiving in-person Bible teaching and testimony.
book.strategy: Group the scattered sessions by doctrinal and practical theme rather than chronology; place exposition before interior discipline, discipline before testimony, and reserve testimony chapters as demonstration of the earlier teaching. Uncertainties are flagged in situ, never resolved.

voice.teaching_style: Instructional, exhortative preacher's voice mixing expository Bible teaching, personal testimony, and pastoral correction
distinctive_traits: Instructional, exhortative preacher's voice mixing expository Bible teaching, personal testimony, and pastoral correction

chapter.p: Resolve the fear-of-death thread opened in the resurrection chapters.
chapter.sum: No fear of death, fear as the devil's old strategy, death as gain lived rather than recited, peaceful departures.

sections.p: Convert the doctrine of destroyed death into lived attitude.

ideas.sum: Believers should not fear death since there is no set time and going to heaven should bring joy, not fear.
Living is abused when death is feared; fear of death is the devil's old strategy.
Death as gain must become one's lived reality, not merely an intellectual idea.
Fear of death observed even among believers reveals it is not yet fully embraced as gain.
If a believer does not practice Christ as life, facing death becomes heavy and difficult.
Some believers foreknow the exact hour of their death and depart peacefully.
